newsitem.title: UK: IPE says will clarify gas oil delivery change.
newsitem.headline: IPE says will clarify gas oil delivery change.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said it would clarify in due course a much-debated change it implemented on Thursday in gas oil delivery regulations.

An IPE spokeswoman said the exchange would issue a clarification to a change to rule J11 which stipulates shorts must have proof of oil in tank when making delivery after each month's contract expiry.
Many traders in Europe welcomed the change, saying it would lessen the likelihood of a repeat of a trading company row which disrupted European heating oil supplies last winter.
The stand-off between Cargill and AIC last November caused a delay in gas oil supplies against expiry of the IPE contract.
But one trader with experience of large deliveries said after learning of the changes on Thursday that he still did not know whether he would still be allowed to deliver third party contracts.
"It's incredible that these rules don't seem to be thought out and that they are pushing them through in a holiday period when many people are away," said a trader in southern Europe.
Traders said two or three other companies had lodged similar objections to the rule change.
"It's poorly done. It seems a shame to have new regulations take effect when no one knows what is deliverable," the trader said.
"Are third party contracts deliverable or not? They were in the past and it seems a shame to forbid something that can amount to 30 to 50 percent of the delivery."
Asked for comment, an IPE spokeswoman said: "This is something they will be issuing guidance on."
The change to J11 was one of seven changes implemented by the IPE and announced in a letter to members.
Three amendments including the change to J11 had aroused concern among members but these were insufficient to block their adoption, the letter said.
The seven approved changes are part of reforms agreed in principle in May by the IPE board of directors and due to take effect in stages during the rest of this year.
The seven changes announced on Thursday will take effect in the September delivery.

Market observers have said the proposed new IPE rules reflect an attempt to strike a balance between keeping traded volumes at a healthy level while guarding against potentially damaging speculative squeezes which can disrupt physical trade.
The most controversial changes involve limits on traders holding large positions ahead of each month's gas oil contract expiry. These are likely to be reviewed, officials say.
Many traders welcomed Thursday's move. "I'm very happy with it," said a Hamburg trader. "The only ones who aren't happy are those who like to mess around with delivery squeezes."
